title: End-to-end embeddings & rerank observability: insights, cost breakdown, and alerting
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Production embeddings + reranking endpoints are becoming a major cost and reliability vector for customers using semantic search and personalized ranking. We currently have coarse telemetry (latency histograms at host level, overall embedding QPS) but lack per-route observability that ties quality regressions, cost, and tail latency to specific routes/model variants. This ticket instruments per-route dashboards, enriches tracing and metric tags, and implements alerting focused on cost anomalies and quality drifts for embeddings/reranking flows.

Goals:
- Add per-route (route_id) dashboards showing latency (P50/P95/P99), throughput, cost per 1k tokens/embeddings, cache hit rate, batch sizing distribution, and model-variant split.
- Surface tracing spans for embedding vectorization and rerank passes (candidate scoring, aggregation) with timing and resource usage.
- Add cost breakdown metrics (tokens_in, tokens_out, gpu_ms, billing_units) tagged by route_id, model_variant, and customer_tier.
- Implement alerting: latency regressions, cost spikes, increased error rates, and embedding-quality drift (via reference prompt synthetic tests).
- Ensure dashboards and alerts are usable for both Hosted and Dedicated customers (respecting data isolation).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change core reranking algorithms or batching implementations. It focuses on observability only.

Success metrics (acceptance criteria):
1) New dashboard template available in Console for any route (template documented and linked).
2) Traces for embeddings and rerank passes appear in 100% of sampled requests with route_id and model_variant tags.
3) Cost-per-route metric (billing_units_per_1k) computed and rolling 24h baseline available.
4) Three alert rules deployed: latency tail (>P95 threshold), 24h cost spike (>2.5x baseline), and embedding-quality drift detected by synthetic checks. Alerts include runbook links.
5) On-call confirmed: an alert triggered in staging and handled end-to-end (incident trace added).

Proposed instrumentation changes (implementation notes):
- Metrics: emit the following metrics with labels: route_id, model_variant, deployment_type (hosted|dedicated), customer_tier, kv_cache_hit (true|false), batch_size_bucket, prefix_len_bucket, embedding_dim. Metrics to emit: embeddings_request_count, embeddings_latency_ms_bucket (histogram), rerank_pass_latency_ms, rerank_score_distribution, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_time_ms, tokens_processed, billing_units.
- Tracing: add explicit spans: span.embed.vectorize, span.embed.kv_lookup, span.rerank.candidate_score (per-batch), span.rerank.aggregate. Each span should tag: route_id, model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_hit. Set sampling rate to 1% globally but 100% for routes marked as 'high_impact' (label on route config).
- Cost breakdown: derive billing_units at request completion using token accounting + GPU_ms * cost_coeff per model_variant. Emit billing_units_per_request metric with same tags. Aggregate to billing_units_per_1k.

Dashboard spec (per-route view):
- Header: route_id, owner, model_variant selector, timeframe selector.
- Row 1: Traffic (QPS), Success rate, Errors/min.
- Row 2: Latency heatmap (P50/P95/P99), histogram of queue time vs compute time, batch size distribution.
- Row 3: Cost: billing_units_per_1k, rolling 24h cost trend, top 5 customers by cost (when permitted).
- Row 4: Quality signals: synthetic evaluation pass rate (reference prompts), mean cosine similarity drift, rerank NDCG change over baseline.
- Row 5: Tracing waterfall sample and top N slow traces with annotated spans.

Alerting rules (initial set):
- A1: Route P95 latency > 200ms for 5m AND traffic > 5 rps -> Severity P1.
- A2: Billing_units in last 24h > 2.5x rolling 7d median -> Severity P2.
- A3: Error rate > 1% for 10m OR sudden increase from baseline (Z-score > 4) -> Severity P0.
- A4: Synthetic evaluation fail rate > 10% drop vs baseline for 1h -> Severity P0.
Each alert to include runbook link and suggested first actions (check batch_size, kv_cache_hit, model_variant rollout).

Quality monitoring (synthetic tests):
- Create a small suite of 50 reference prompts per route (seeded by PMs/owners). Run every 15m in staging and every hour in prod with low QPS. Emit pass_rate and embedding_cosine_drift. Tie alerts to these metrics.

Rollout plan:
1) Instrumentation + metrics + tracing in a feature branch (ENG-8602/instrumentation).
2) Deploy metrics to staging for a subset of routes (select 5 high-impact routes).
3) Create dashboard template and alert rules in staging; iterate with on-call.
4) Gradually enable tracing sampling 100% for high-impact routes and 1% elsewhere.
5) Deploy to prod with monitoring and a one-week watch.

Testing & validation:
- End-to-end test that verifies billing_units computed correctly (unit tests + integration test).
- Synthetic test run triggers alert in staging to exercise runbooks.
- Load testing at expected 3x peak to validate cardinality and metric pipeline saturation.

Deliverables:
- Instrumentation PRs (runtime + router + metrics exporter).
- Console dashboard template (JSON) and documentation page.
- Alert rules & runbooks.
- Synthetic prompt sets for first 20 routes and a script to add more.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/38723/embeddings-rerank-observability
- Draft dashboard template (Gist): https://gist.github.com/redwood/emb-rerank-dashboard
- PoC tracing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2418
- Billing derivation notebook: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h/view

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Cardinality: tagging every request by route_id and customer_id will raise cardinality; we propose route_id + customer_tier only in metrics and include customer_id only for sampled logs (not metrics).
- Sampling: tracing 100% for high-impact routes increases storage; need to size traces store and add retention policy.
- Synthetic tests coverage: how many reference prompts per route are sufficient to detect embedding drift without false positives? Start at 50 and iterate.
